headline: Managing Seasonal Resort Access and Mountain Lodging
reservation: Winter lift tickets and summer activity passes often require early online purchase for better availability. Peak season lodging in the village and glamping sites in the Eagle River Valley should be secured months ahead; check official resort sites for changing reservation policies.

days.title: Alpine Flora and Village Culture

stops.name: Betty Ford Alpine Gardens
stops.detail: Stroll through the world's highest botanical gardens featuring unique high-altitude plant species.

stops.name: Vail Village
stops.detail: Explore the pedestrian-friendly, European-inspired streets and the Colorado Snowsports Museum.

days.driving: Local walking and shuttle use recommended; conditions vary
days.note: Use the free town bus to navigate between Vail Village and Lionshead to avoid parking congestion.

days.title: Summit Vistas and High Trails

stops.name: Eagle Bahn Gondola
stops.detail: Ascend to Eagle's Nest for panoramic views of the Mount of the Holy Cross and the Gore Range.

stops.name: Berry Picker Trail
stops.detail: Hike the scenic switchbacks through aspen groves, choosing to walk up or ride the gondola down.

days.driving: Minimal driving required if staying in town; conditions vary
days.note: Gondola operations are seasonal; verify summer vs. winter dates before arrival.

days.title: River Canyons and High Desert

stops.name: Gore Creek
stops.detail: Visit Gold Medal fishing waters for a morning of fly fishing or a quiet riverside walk.

stops.name: Colorado River Road
stops.detail: Drive toward the red rock canyons west of Wolcott for a different geological perspective of the region.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for regional exploring; conditions vary
days.note: River levels fluctuate with spring snowmelt; check local flow reports for water activities.

intel.title: Village Structure Rates
intel.text: Parking structures in Vail Village and Lionshead are free for short periods in summer but expensive in winter. Utilize the free park-and-ride lots to avoid high daily fees.

intel.title: High Country Dead Zones
intel.text: Expect signal loss on trails within the Holy Cross Wilderness and along remote sections of the Trough Road. Carry a physical map for backcountry hiking.

intel.title: I-70 Corridor Services
intel.text: Fuel is plentiful in Vail, Eagle, and Silverthorne, but prices can be significantly higher in the resort core. Fill up in larger gateway towns like Denver or Grand Junction if driving in.

intel.title: Altitude Acclimatization
intel.text: Plan strenuous hikes for later in your trip to allow for elevation adjustment. Afternoon thunderstorms are common in summer; aim to be below the treeline by noon.

intel.title: Vail Pass Conditions
intel.text: I-70 over Vail Pass can close abruptly due to snow or accidents. Check CDOT's COTrip website for real-time mountain pass status.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at Eagle County Regional (EGE), stop for groceries in Eagle, and arrive at your mountain lodge for evening check-in.
plan.vehicle: A vehicle with AWD/4WD and high clearance is recommended for winter or unpaved forest roads; check local traction laws.
plan.goldenHour: Enjoy Eagle Bahn Gondola summit views during scheduled scenic operating hours and confirm the last downhill ride before boarding; do not assume the gondola operates through sunset.
